summary: Sticky pin cache TTL exceeded after regional canary rollback causing session fallback loop
description: Issue summary: After a regional canary rollback in us-east, some PhotonPay sessions remained pinned to the canary variant and continued to route to an evicted serving group. The edge route cache honored a stale sticky-pin token with an extended TTL, which caused the routing layer to repeatedly attempt the pinned variant and trigger fallback logic. Impact: PhotonPay reported elevated 5xxs and long tail latency on customer-facing calls (~3–5% error rate for affected sessions) and inability for affected users to reach their pinned model until sessions were cleared. Environment: Dedicated pool for PhotonPay in prod/us-east; canary weight toggled then rolled back during 2026-03-09 22:00–22:15 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a canary for rwd-opus-v1 on PhotonPay dedicated pool with weight 10% in us-east.
2) Establish a long-lived session (session token / affinity cookie) to the pinned canary variant and confirm model responses.
3) Roll the canary back to stable (weight 0) via Console -> Rollouts at 2026-03-09 22:12 UTC.
4) Observe that session traffic continues to include X-Model-Pin header for the canary variant and is routed using edge cache entries with TTL > pin TTL.

5) The serving runtime evicted the canary worker nodes at 22:14 UTC; requests return 502/504 and fallback controller repeatedly tries alternate variants, causing repeated transient 5xx and high latency.
6) Clearing the session (new session token) restores normal routing to stable model.

investigation: Initial triage by Support (Priya): customer reported persistent 5xxs after canary rollback; reproduces for sessions created before rollback.
SRE (Evan) collected traces and saw edge-proxy route-cache entries with TTL=7200s (2h) while pin tokens had TTL=300s; mismatch allowed stale cache entries to outlive model availability.

Engineering hypothesis: when canary was rolled back rapidly, canary-controller issued eviction but edge-proxy had previously cached route entries that included stamped pin metadata. On cache refresh, a bug in cache revalidation preserved the pin header and extended TTL using cache rehydration codepath (introduced in edge-proxy PR #1259).

Confirmed root cause: route-cache rehydration path inadvertently copied X-Model-Pin from cached metadata during a rollback event and set cache-ttl based on route policy rather than pin expiry. Combined with immediate decommissioning of canary workers, this led to repeated attempts to reach an unavailable variant and triggered fallback loops.

Scope: Customer-scoped (PhotonPay) dedicated pool and a small subset of session tokens created in the 20-minute window prior to rollback. Estimated affected sessions: ~4k, affecting ~3% of PhotonPay's requests during the incident window.
Cross references: Slack #support (https://slack.redwood.ai/support), ops-runbook note, and related ticket SUP-31147 (session-resume-drops-version-affinity-causes-fallback).
Temporary mitigation discussed: avoid immediate decommissioning of canary workers until pinned sessions age out OR invalidate pinned tokens actively on rollback for affected tenants.
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Desai (Support): Logged initial report from PhotonPay CS. Customer reports that users in certain sessions see repeated 502s after canary revert. Asked SRE to collect traces and advise workaround.

2026-03-10 Evan Black (SRE): Collected edge traces and confirmed route-cache TTL/pin TTL mismatch. Placed a short-term mitigation: added tenant-level cache invalidation signal (manual) to edge-proxy for PhotonPay to flush stale route entries.

2026-03-11 Marco Rivera (Eng - Edge): Identified codepath introduced in PR #1259 that copies pin metadata on rehydration. Preparing hotfix PR to stop copying X-Model-Pin when cached target is unhealthy or when rollback event flag is present.

2026-03-11 Customer (PhotonPay - CS): After Support requested session reset, customer cleared sessions via Console and reported error rate dropped to <0.1%. Asked for permanent fix and verification plan.

2026-03-12 Evan Black (SRE): Hotfix deployed to canary edge-proxies in us-east (edge-proxy PR #1287). Running targeted migration to invalidate pinned tokens for PhotonPay; monitoring shows errors back to baseline.
2026-03-12 Priya Desai (Support): Notified customer of fix and asked for confirmation of restored behavior and permission to close incident after 24h observation.
2026-03-12 PhotonPay (CS): Confirmed normal behavior; requested root-cause writeup and runbook update for future canary rollbacks.
resolution: Short-term workaround: Support instructed customer to clear affected sessions (Console -> Sessions -> Invalidate) or rotate session tokens; we provided an automated script to invalidate session pins for Tenant=PhotonPay.

Hotfix: Edge-proxy PR #1287 prevents route-cache rehydration from copying X-Model-Pin metadata when target health != HEALTHY or when a rollback flag is set. Hotfix deployed to us-east edge fleet on 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC.
Migration: Ran tenant-scoped token invalidation job for PhotonPay (job id: mz-inval-20260312-photonpay) to remove stale pins from session-store and route-cache.
Monitoring & verification: Post-deploy dashboard shows 99.95% success rate for PhotonPay requests and 95th percentile latency returned to baseline within 40 minutes.

Follow-ups: 
      - Update canary rollback runbook to include explicit pin invalidation step (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/canary-rollbacks).
- Add unit/integration tests to edge-proxy to ensure pin metadata is not persisted across rollbacks (tracked in GH issue #1310).
- Consider adding a TTL reconciliation job that ensures pin TTL <= route-cache TTL for tenant-scoped caches.

Customer communication: Customer notified, requested postmortem; assigned to Eng for a brief RCA doc and runbook update. Customer asked for a follow-up review in 1 week to validate rollout safety improvements.
